The add-attribute path is a per-attribute REST call, not the visit save. The frontend POSTs to `/visit/{uuid}/attribute`, and the REST layer ends in `VisitService.saveVisit`, which persists through `HibernateVisitDAO.saveVisit`.

1. **Frontend request:** `createVisitAttribute` POSTs `{ attributeType, value }` to `${restBaseUrl}/visit/${visitUuid}/attribute` (`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-form/visit-form.resource.ts:172-178`). Editing an existing attribute goes through `updateVisitAttribute`, which POSTs to `/visit/{uuid}/attribute/{attributeUuid}` (same file, 180-186). The visit form calls `updateVisitAttribute` for existing attributes (`exported-visit-form.workspace.tsx:217`). I did not confirm which function the form calls for a brand-new attribute on an existing visit, so the create-versus-update routing is the one part I'm inferring.
2. **REST handler:** `MainSubResourceController.create` maps `POST /{resource}/{parentUuid}/{subResource}` and looks up the `visit/attribute` subresource (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/.../v1_0/controller/MainSubResourceController.java:117-127`).
3. **REST resource logic:** `DelegatingSubResource.create` loads the parent visit, builds the delegate, applies the posted properties, then calls `save` (`.../omod-common/.../resource/impl/DelegatingSubResource.java:87-98`). `VisitAttributeResource1_9.save` adds the attribute to the visit and calls `Context.getVisitService().saveVisit(visit)` (`.../omod/.../openmrs1_9/VisitAttributeResource1_9.java:97-116`). The `value` property is converted by `BaseAttributeCrudResource1_9.setValue` (lines 49-55).
4. **Core service:** `VisitServiceImpl.saveVisit` checks the ADD_VISITS or EDIT_VISITS privilege, calls `CustomDatatypeUtil.saveAttributesIfNecessary(visit)`, then calls `dao.saveVisit` (`openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/VisitServiceImpl.java:178-187`).
5. **Data access:** `HibernateVisitDAO.saveVisit` returns `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate(getCurrentSession(), visit)` (`openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateVisitDAO.java:167-169`). I did not read the session flush or commit, so the exact moment the row is written is unverified.

The save also has a second entry point. When a new visit is created with attributes, the form sends them inline in the `saveVisit` payload instead (`exported-visit-form.workspace.tsx:285-324`). I did not trace that server path.

I did not trace the update and delete paths in full. I used the entire search budget, so I could not confirm `DelegatingSubResource.update` routes to `save`.
